notes:
Summary: late-stage procurement, POC completed but failed to satisfy burst-tail SLOs. Key ask was live-chat/agent assist with strict tail-latency targets and unpredictable bursts from device telemetry.

Call snippets / quotes: 'We need predictable responses during surge events — customers are on the line.'; 'If 99.9th jumps, ops gets paged and we lose SLAs.'

POC highlights: ran dedicated POC for chat_support + alerting. Workload profile: sustained 400-500 QPS for embeddings+chat with regionally concentrated bursts to ~800 QPS for 30-90s windows. Desired SLOs: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 350ms, p99.9 < 500ms (hard).

Redwood POC results: p95 ~120ms (ok), p99 ~320ms (borderline), p99.9 spiked to ~540ms under synthetic burst scenario due to queueing and KV-cache cold starts. Observed queue depth growth when multiple long-context sessions hit simultaneously. SE notes: kernel-selection and batching configuration good for steady state but burst tail suffers without aggressive overprovisioning or faster autoscale.

Customer reaction: concerned about cost of provisioning headroom vs. risk. Procurement pushed back on Dedicated sizing that would guarantee tail SLAs; security wanted autoscaling proof that didn't leak logs across instances (VPC/on-prem preferred).

Competitive pressure: Customer cited Anthropic offering a managed autoscaling pitch with a multi-region failover demo; procurement perceived lower ramp cost.

Outcome: After three follow-ups and a final SOW revision request, hiring/budget freeze announced (velocity team restructured). Customer moved to 'pause' then elected competitor in April. Marked closed-lost; keep resources for potential re-engage.

technical_summary: Technical fit: moderate functional fit for chat/reranking, but poor fit on burst tail guarantees under current cost constraints. POC showed steady throughput OK; queueing and KV-cache cold starts cause p99.9 violations under burst windows. Recommended mitigations (not accepted): pre-warmed dedicated nodes, conservative autoscale buffer, region-based routing, prefix/KV caching tuning. Customer unwilling to accept required ARR uplift to guarantee headroom.
